clue.text: The servant standing behind the 1st Earl of Ypres is a foreigner

indicators.note: the servant stands behind the earl, so his word comes after the earl's surname

parts.note: Field Marshal Sir John French was created the first Earl of Ypres after the First World War
a man is a manservant, a valet or butler

explanation.surface: A footman waits behind a First World War earl, and turns out to be from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Earl of Ypres sounds like a Belgian title, but it was given to the British commander John French.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from across the Channel is one kind of foreigner to a British setter.

clue.text: Source of power used by Eliot's mill to make silk

definitions.text: Source of power used by Eliot's mill
definitions.meaning: George Eliot's novel The Mill on the ___ names the river that drives the mill's wheel
rough silk fibres used for embroidery thread

explanation.surface: Power from the mill in a George Eliot novel produces silk.
explanation.walkthrough: The water mill in George Eliot's novel is driven by the river named in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: A river turns a mill wheel, and the same word names loose silk fibre used in embroidery.

clue.text: Key singer carried by motor yacht to a diplomat's residence

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: the singer is carried inside the yacht, so the boat's letters go round it

parts.note: MY is the abbreviation for motor yacht, put before a vessel's name
a bass is a singer with the lowest voice

explanation.surface: A deep-voiced singer is carried by motorboat to the ambassador's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like the start of the definition, but it is just a musical key; 'carried by' signals a container, the yacht holding the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador's official home and office abroad.

clue.text: Record animal on a tree-trunk for listeners

indicators.note: for listeners means the pieces are to be heard, giving the sound of the word

parts.note: a cat is the animal, then a, and a log is a cut tree-trunk; in a down clue the cat sits on top

explanation.surface: A cat on a log is recorded for people listening in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for listeners' says CAT A LOG sounds like the answer, though spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A list or register of items, such as a library's index, is a kind of record.

clue.text: Philosopher on island displayed anger at his riches…

definitions.text: Philosopher on island displayed anger at his riches

indicators.note: in a down clue the philosopher sits on top of the island

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a British philosopher
Iona is a small island in the Scottish Hebrides
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A thinker on a remote island is angry about how wealthy he has become.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue pictures a rich man; the definition is loose, leaning on 'his riches'. The ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose riches run to a seven-figure sum is very wealthy.

clue.text: … and not in an orderly manner!

indicators.note: in shows that the letters wanted are tucked inside the next words of the clue

explanation.surface: The sentence from the previous clue runs on: and not in a tidy fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'aN ORderly'. The ellipsis links the surface to the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction that continues a negative, as in neither this nor that, means and not.

clue.text: Doctor and accountant drinking hot coffee

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a military doctor

indicators.note: the doctor and accountant take the hot letter into themselves, as if swallowing it

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A doctor and an accountant sip a hot cup of coffee together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts H inside MOCA, the doctor and accountant joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong Arabian-style coffee, often flavoured with chocolate, takes its name from a Yemeni port.

clue.text: Cat extremely useful to a person of influence

parts.note: mog or moggy is British slang for a cat

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of useful

explanation.surface: A cat is very handy to an important person.
explanation.walkthrough: MOG is British slang for an ordinary house cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mogul emperor ruled India, so the word came to mean a powerful magnate.

clue.text: Bring out leader of refrain, being once such a singer

definitions.text: Bring out leader of refrain, being once such a singer

parts.words: Bring out leader of refrain, being once such a singer
parts.note: take the first letter of refrain out of Bring and you are left with Bing, the first name of Crosby, a famous soft-voiced singer of the past

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like an instruction to sing, but removing R from BRING leaves BING, as in Bing Crosby, the style of singer wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing Crosby was the best-known exponent of soft, intimate popular singing.

clue.text: Hang on without her being up-set, understand?

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the attaching word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to append is to attach or hang something on

indicators.note: up-set in a down clue means set upside down, so the word her is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you understand that she is upset when left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and the hyphen in 'up-set' points to turning a word upside down in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp the meaning of something is to comprehend it.

clue.text: It's said to guard part of a drill moving around

indicators.note: the spoken word stands either side of the drill part, as a guard surrounds what it protects

parts.note: oral means spoken, said rather than written
a bit is the cutting tip fitted to a drill

explanation.surface: Something is said to protect a piece of a drill that keeps spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' suggests a sound-alike, but 'said' simply gives ORAL, which guards BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving in an orbit goes round and round another body, as a satellite does.

clue.text: Alter formation of army pop musicians

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a pop group is a band of musicians

explanation.surface: A military band changes its line-up, as soldiers and pop musicians might.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather again in fresh order is to change how troops or people are formed up.

clue.text: The girl outside is of this fibre!

indicators.note: the girl's name sits round the outside of the little word from the clue

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: A young woman exclaims that she is made of this cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The girl' asks for a short girl's name; 'outside' says it wraps the clue's own 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff plant fibre from an agave is used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Laziness causes no decline, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of these words are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A claim that idleness stops a person's decline, which is odd advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' tells you to rearrange the letters of NO DECLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness and sloth are other words for laziness, a reluctance to work.

clue.text: He makes plans, moving about on board

definitions.meaning: a person who draws technical plans and designs
a piece in the game of draughts, called checkers in the US, moving across the board

explanation.surface: A planner paces around on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but it is a draughts board; a draughts piece can go by the same name as a plan-drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughts piece and a technical drawer share one name, each a different sense.

clue.text: Might presently exclude border from violent action

indicators.note: the border's word is left out of the violent word, leaving what remains

parts.note: mayhem is violent disorder or destruction
a hem is the folded border of a cloth

explanation.surface: Violence might soon be kept away from the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exclude' removes HEM from MAYHEM. 'presently' turns the past-tense 'might' into its present form.
explanation.definitionFit: The modal verb of possibility has a past tense 'might' and a present tense of three letters.

clue.text: Margaret Herbert has one for distant communication

parts.note: Meg is a short form of Margaret
A. P. Herbert was an English humorist and MP, known by his initials
taken as written

explanation.surface: Margaret and Herbert share one device for speaking at a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert is A. P. Herbert, the twentieth-century English humorist, who gives his initials APH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped horn amplifies the voice so it carries to listeners far off.

clue.text: Police in terrible danger — one is thrown in lake

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of danger are thrown into disorder
one is thrown into the lake, so its letter goes inside

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In great danger, one person is thrown into a lake by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DANGER into GENDAR; 'is thrown in' puts I into MERE to give MERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French armed police force is a body of gendarmes.

clue.text: Preserve Sandhurst youth in West

indicators.note: the academy and the youth are placed inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was an American film actress
Sandhurst is the Royal Military Academy, RMA, where British army officers train
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A Sandhurst cadet is kept safe in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction but is the American actress Mae West; 'in' says the academy and the youth go inside her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus jam, typically of Seville oranges, is a preserve.

clue.text: Unsmiling Australian working in God's acre

parts.note: grave means serious, solemn, unsmiling
a digger is informal for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: A stern Australian is busy in a churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: God's acre is an old name for a churchyard; the definition describes who works there, digging plots.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchyard labourer prepares the burial plots, so that is the work done in God's acre.

clue.text: Dreadful article written before you and I part

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are written before the word for part

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
you and I together are we
some means a part or portion

explanation.surface: A dreadful article is written before two people go their separate ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring dread or awe is the older sense of a word now mostly used for 'great'.

clue.text: It introduces a large number down in the dumps

indicators.note: it comes first and introduces the number that follows

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Something introduces a big figure to someone feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for SA (sex appeal) is an old crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down in the dumps is being unhappy or miserable.

clue.text: Law, say, restricting you in Paris

indicators.note: the word for say restricts, holding the French word inside it

parts.note: to state is to say
tu is the French for you

explanation.surface: A law, so to speak, restricts what you can do in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you in Paris' asks for the French word, and 'restricting' says the word for say holds it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Republican leader given donation out of the state

indicators.note: the donation is placed outside the state, wrapping around it

parts.note: a present is a gift or donation
ID is the postal abbreviation for Idaho, a US state

explanation.surface: The head of a party is given a gift from outside the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is read as outside, so the gift wraps round the state; the state is Idaho by its postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of state of a republic holds the highest office, as in the USA or France.

clue.text: Key used by Novello coming to end of play

parts.note: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor

indicators.note: the end of the word play is its last letter

explanation.surface: A piano key played by Novello at the close of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and matinee idol of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally faced with elephant tusk, so the word means a piano key.

clue.text: Gather for a service

parts.note: Mass is the service of the Eucharist in the Catholic church

explanation.surface: People come together for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect or accumulate, as one gathers a fortune.

clue.text: Place in which he produced a newspaper

indicators.note: the place word is the one in which the little pronoun is put

parts.note: to set is to place

explanation.surface: The place where a man once ran a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' is used as it is, and 'in which' says the word for place holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is often slangily called a sheet, a single printed paper.

clue.text: Starts to offer lots of rosé, or sometimes of sherry

indicators.note: the starts of these words are their first letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: A wine list offers plenty of rosé, or now and then some sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first letter of each of the seven words from 'offer' to the second 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark, sweet-leaning Spanish fortified wine is one style of sherry.

clue.text: German physicist mostly serving a British monarch?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: OHMS stands for On Her (or His) Majesty's Service, printed on official British mail

explanation.surface: Asking whether a German scientist mostly works for the British Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: OHMS, On Her Majesty's Service, is printed on British government envelopes; 'mostly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Simon Ohm was the German physicist who gave his name to the unit of resistance.

clue.text: Dance for which Shakespeare wrote this?

definitions.meaning: a stately dance of the Elizabethan era
Shakespeare's comedy title is one word, then 'for', then the same word again, so the word is what he wrote 'for'

explanation.surface: Asking which dance Shakespeare wrote a piece for.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the title of Shakespeare's comedy, whose name is the same word twice with 'for' between.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave Elizabethan dance shares its name with a quantity, and with a Shakespeare play title.

clue.text: A plaintive song, say, in the old isle

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the middle of the isle's name

parts.note: the Isle of Ely in Cambridgeshire was once an island in the fens
eg means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: A sad song, for example, sung on an ancient island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Ely is an English district that was an island before the fens around it were drained.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful poem or song, especially a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Pie-filling many in the pit encounter, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken and their sound gives the answer

parts.note: many pits are mines, and encounter means meet, so the phrase gives mines meet

explanation.surface: A crowd of miners meet over the filling of a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' tells you to say MINES MEET out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet mix of dried fruit, suet and spice is what fills a Christmas pie in Britain.
